content.prompt: Identify the solutions using the null factor law.

answer.worked:
Both factors give the same equation.
$$\begin{aligned}x+3&=0\\x&=-3\end{aligned}$$

Since $2\ne0$, the other factor must be zero.
$$\begin{aligned}x+3&=0\\x&=-3\end{aligned}$$

content.prompt: Write an equation and solve it to find the number.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The square of the number is 7 times the same number

answer.worked:
Let the number be $x$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=7x\\x^2-7x&=0\\x(x-7)&=0\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=0$ or $x-7=0$.
Hence $x=0$ or $7$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The difference between the square of a number and 64 is zero.

children.label: c
children.prompt: 3 times the square of a number is equal to $-12$ times the number.

answer.worked:
Let the number be $x$.
$$\begin{align*}3x^2&=-12x\\3x^2+12x&=0\\3x(x+4)&=0\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=0$ or $x+4=0$.
Hence $x=0$ or $-4$.

answer.worked:
Since $x\ne0$, multiply by $x$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2-4&=0\\x^2&=4\\x&=\pm2\end{align*}$$
Both values are nonzero.

Since $x\ne0$, multiply by $x$.
$$\begin{align*}36-x^2&=0\\x^2&=36\\x&=\pm6\end{align*}$$
Both values are nonzero.

Since $x\ne0$, multiply by $x^2$.
$$\begin{align*}3&=3x^2\\x^2&=1\\x&=\pm1\end{align*}$$
Both values are nonzero.

$$\begin{align*}x^2-3x&=2x^2+4x\\x^2+7x&=0\\x(x+7)&=0\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=0$ or $x+7=0$.
Hence $x=0$ or $-7$.

$$\begin{align*}15x-3x^2&=7x-x^2\\2x^2-8x&=0\\2x(x-4)&=0\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=0$ or $x-4=0$.
Hence $x=0$ or $4$.

content.prompt: An equation of the form $ax^2+bx=0$ will always have two solutions if $a$ and $b$ are not zero.

children.label: a
children.prompt: By factorising the LHS, explain why one of the solutions will always be $x=0$.

answer.short: $x(ax+b)=0$. The factor $x$ is zero when $x=0$, so $x=0$ is always a solution.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}ax^2+bx&=0\\x(ax+b)&=0\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=0$ or $ax+b=0$. Therefore $x=0$ is always a solution.

answer.short: $x=-8$. Since $(x+8)^{2}=0$, both factors give the same solution.
answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}(x+8)^{2}&=0\\x+8&=0\\x&=-8\end{align*}$

The trinomial is a perfect square. Both factors are $x+8$, so there is only one distinct solution.

answer.short: General form: $x^2+x-6=0$; factors: $3,-2$; factorised form: $(x+3)(x-2)=0$; solutions: $x=-3$ or $2$.
answer.worked:
$3+(-2)=1$ and $3(-2)=-6$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2+x-6&=0\\(x+3)(x-2)&=0\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=-3$ or $2$.

answer.short: General form: $x^2-4x=0$; sum: $-4$; product: $0$; factors: $0,-4$; factorised form: $x(x-4)=0$.
answer.worked:
The solutions give factors $x$ and $x-4$.
$$\begin{align*}x(x-4)&=0\\x^2-4x&=0\end{align*}$$
The factor constants are $0,-4$; their sum is $-4$ and product is $0$.

answer.short: General form: $x^2-16x+64=0$; sum: $-16$; product: $64$; factors: $-8,-8$; factorised form: $(x-8)^2=0$.
answer.worked:
The repeated solution $x=8$ gives two factors $x-8$.
$$\begin{align*}(x-8)^2&=0\\x^2-16x+64&=0\end{align*}$$
The factor constants are $-8,-8$; their sum is $-16$ and product is $64$.

answer.short: Sum: $0$; product: $-4$; factors: $-2,2$; factorised form: $(x-2)(x+2)=0$; solutions: $x=\pm2$.
answer.worked:
$-2+2=0$ and $(-2)(2)=-4$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2-4&=0\\(x-2)(x+2)&=0\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=2$ or $-2$.

answer.short: General form: $x^2-6x+9=0$; sum: $-6$; product: $9$; factors: $-3,-3$; factorised form: $(x-3)^2=0$.
answer.worked:
The repeated solution $x=3$ gives two factors $x-3$.
$$\begin{align*}(x-3)^2&=0\\x^2-6x+9&=0\end{align*}$$
The factor constants are $-3,-3$; their sum is $-6$ and product is $9$.

answer.short: Sum: $-12$; product: $36$; factors: $-6,-6$; factorised form: $(x-6)^2=0$; solution: $x=6$ only.
answer.worked:
$(-6)+(-6)=-12$ and $(-6)(-6)=36$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2-12x+36&=0\\(x-6)^2&=0\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=6$ only.

answer.short: General form: $x^2-9=0$; sum: $0$; product: $-9$; factors: $-3,3$; factorised form: $(x-3)(x+3)=0$.
answer.worked:
The solutions give factors $x-3$ and $x+3$.
$$\begin{align*}(x-3)(x+3)&=0\\x^2-9&=0\end{align*}$$
The factor constants are $-3,3$; their sum is $0$ and product is $-9$.

answer.short: General form: $x^2-2x+1=0$; sum: $-2$; product: $1$; factors: $-1,-1$; solution: $x=1$ only.
answer.worked:
$(-1)+(-1)=-2$ and $(-1)(-1)=1$.
$$\begin{align*}(x-1)^2&=0\\x^2-2x+1&=0\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=1$ only.

answer.short: Sum: $0$; product: $-1$; factors: $1,-1$; factorised form: $(x-1)(x+1)=0$; solutions: $x=\pm1$.
answer.worked:
$1+(-1)=0$ and $1(-1)=-1$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2-1&=0\\(x-1)(x+1)&=0\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law, $x=1$ or $-1$.

classification.difficultyReason: Set the temperature expression equal to zero and interpret the roots as clock times.

content.prompt:
The temperature in °C inside a room at a base in Antarctica is given by the expression $t^{2}-9t+8$, where $t$ is hours after 10 am.
Find the times in the day when the temperature is 0°C.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}t^{2}-9t+8&=0\\(t-8)(t-1)&=0\\t&=1\text{ or }8\end{align*}$$
The temperature is 0°C at 11 am and 6 pm.
